review_q_rulings: Q2 (rule scope: only tools/**/*.py, not tests/ or root scripts): RULING = AGREE with the boundary, with two measured caveats. (a) The distinction is production-tooling vs one-shot CI test environment, and widening is how a guard turns into noise - the author's stated reason holds. (b) Measured evidence the boundary is defensible: there are NO *.py scripts at the repo root (Get-ChildItem *.py is empty), so 'root scripts not scanned' has zero current surface. (c) Measured counter-example the author did NOT list: tests/test_check_owned_files.py:247 is a live `subprocess.run([...], capture_output=True, text=True)` with NO encoding - the same defect class - it is safe today only because the test environment is UTF-8 and git-config output is ASCII. test_pre_push_hook.py's _popen avoids it by force-injecting encoding='utf-8' (L188 kw.setdefault). So 'only tools/' is correct, but the reviewer records that the class still has one live instance in tests/ that a full-repo scan WOULD have caught - it is a latent, not a false-positive-justified, exemption. Logged as advisory A2, not required.

Q3 (BOM hole: is utf-8-sig right; any other silent-skip path?): RULING = the utf-8-sig fix is CORRECT (reviewer's BOM sample is now flagged, not skipped; BOM test at L1716 pins it). But YES, there is another silent-skip path the author did not name: the rule reads source with `errors="replace"` and then `except SyntaxError: continue` - so any tools/**.py that cannot be strictly parsed is silently abandoned with ZERO finding and ZERO notice. Today that surface is 0 (all 17 tools/**.py parse clean under utf-8-sig, reviewer measured), so it is potential not live - but it directly contradicts the repo's own stated iron rule at docs/lint-rules.md L466-467 ('A missing anchor is an error, never a silent no-op. A tool that reports success while changing nothing is the failure mode this whole exercise targets'). A file that stops parsing would silently stop being guarded, with no signal. RULING: not a blocker (surface=0 today, fixing it is a design choice - report an ERROR finding vs skip - not a checkout detail), logged as advisory A1 with a recommended follow-up.

Q4 (policy wording: '_handoffs is also a git repo, so it is really repo-to-repo - will the phrasing mislead future readers into thinking there is no version control?): RULING = the phrasing as written WOULD mislead, but in the OPPOSITE direction from the author's worry. It does not understate version control; it overstates durability. _handoffs is a git repo (HEAD advanced to 206b336) but has NO remote (git remote -v empty), so 'EVO verdicts live in _handoffs' currently means 'version-controlled in a local-only repo, no remote backup, one machine's disk' - strictly weaker than the pre-move 'tracked in covenant' for disaster recovery. RULING: add a half-sentence so a future reader is not led to assume durability they do not have: 'version control is local-only (_handoffs has no remote); if multi-machine/backup is ever needed, _handoffs must gain a remote.' Also noted: index.json still carries two STALE verdict_refs (EVO-20261010-006, EVO-20261014-001) pointing at the now-deleted agent-covenant/verdicts/... paths - pre-005 leftovers, out of this card's scope, logged as advisory A3.
